next_step: Run dedicated capacity sizing workshop; customer to upload 14 days of production traffic telemetry and p99 latency histograms; draft SOW after sizing.
notes:
Lead: Alyssa Chen (AE). SE: Diego Morales. CSM: Priya Nair.

Account summary:
- Mid-stage adtech platform focused on realtime personalization and reranking for bidding and creative choice. High QPS bursts during sales hours; global footprint but compliance-first (EU/NA data residency).
- Strong ops team, already operates a subset of models in-house for A/B experiments; looking to offload production serving to Redwood Dedicated for predictability and cost control.

Technical requirements (from discovery calls):
- Baseline QPS: ~50 sustained QPS for personalization API (avg 2–3 concurrent requests per user flow).
- Average token/request: 25–40 tokens (short prompts + context + response).
- Baseline tokens/sec estimate: 50 QPS * 30 tokens ≈ 1,500 tokens/sec.
- Peak burst: 180–220 QPS during ad auctions windows -> peak tokens/sec ≈ 6,000–8,800 (depend on token distribution).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms for 1k token budgets; 50–100ms additional allowance for network.
- Throughput guarantees desired for business-critical endpoint; customer wants committed reserved GPU capacity with clear throughput and fallback model routing when overloaded.

POC / Sizing considerations discussed in calls:
- Need a dedicated capacity sizing workshop to map their real traffic histogram to Redwood GPU sizing. Important inputs: request size distribution, batching opportunities, KV cache hit rates, prefix pattern reuse, and traffic seasonality.
- They prefer conservative reserve with burst credits for traffic spikes rather than pure autoscaling.
- Discussed model variants: prefer open models (Llama-variant and mix of proprietary reranker) but will accept Redwood-curated quantized variants if quality is preserved.
- KMS integration and audit logging mandatory; SSO / SAML required for console access.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-18: Intro demo + Q&A (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_9a7b2c).
- 2026-02-25: Security pre-screen call; customer submitted initial security questionnaire (drive:/deals/fjordscale/security-faq.docx).
- 2026-03-02: Follow-up architecture deep-dive with SE. Customer agreed to provide 14-day traffic dump and sample p95/p99 histograms.
- 2026-03-05: AE updated with preliminary throughput targets and requested workshop dates.

Open items / Risks:
- Need to align on which model variants Redwood will guarantee throughput for (full precision vs quantized).
- Procurement asks for CAPEX-style committed spend; finance needs clear SLO->capacity->price mapping to approve.
- Network egress and cross-region latency for EU users must be validated in Private/VPC deployment.

Next steps (short):
- Schedule 90-minute dedicated capacity sizing workshop (SE + customer infra + RD team) week of 2026-03-15.
- Customer to upload 14 days of request traces and token distribution CSV to shared drive by 2026-03-10.
- Post-workshop: Redwood to produce a recommended reserved GPU plan (capacity table: baseline vs burst), expected p95/p99, cost estimate, and SOW draft.

Sales remarks:
- High likelihood to convert if sizing workshop shows <40% uplift in cost vs their current infra per unit throughput.
- Recommend proposing 12-month committed Dedicated tier with burst credits and a 30-day canary to validate quantized model outputs.

Quoted preliminary sizing guidance (ballpark for workshop prep only):
- Baseline steady-state: 4–6 A100-80GB or equivalent infer nodes (depending on batching and KV cache efficacy).
- Peak buffer / reserved burst overlap: additional 6–8 GPUs for auction-hour spikes, or alternatively a mixed routing policy to cheaper model variants for non-critical queries.
- These numbers to be validated in workshop; do not finalize without telemetry mapping.

Stated customer priority: "Predictable latency for auction-critical calls; cost control for long tail traffic."
